findings.title: Backup code plus any dummy TOTP code bypasses password verification at login
findings.body: In the credentials authorize callback, the password check is gated on `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)` (line 121): whenever a totpCode value is present, the password is never verified. The new backup-code branch `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)` is evaluated before the TOTP branch, so an attacker can POST to the credentials callback with `email`, `backupCode=<valid code>`, and `totpCode=000000` (any non-empty value) and log in without knowing the account password. The web UI never sends both fields, but nothing server-side prevents it, so a backup code — intended as a second factor after the password — becomes a single-factor credential that fully bypasses the password. The fix should verify the password (when the user has one) regardless of whether totpCode or backupCode is supplied, or reject requests that contain both a backupCode and a totpCode.

findings.title: Backup codes unusable for GOOGLE/SAML users who have 2FA enabled
findings.body: The guard `if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode) throw new Error(ErrorCode.ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled)` runs before the backup-code branch. Users whose identity provider is GOOGLE or SAML but who have twoFactorEnabled — which the signIn callback itself can create by converting a CAL account with 2FA to Google/SAML (lines 693–706) — log in via the loginWithTotp flow, where the password field is empty. If such a user clicks 'Lost access' and submits a backup code, totpCode is empty, so they get ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled ('account_created_with_identity_provider') instead of the backup code being checked. These users can never use their backup codes and are locked out if they lose their authenticator. The identity-provider guards need to treat a supplied backupCode the same way as a totpCode.

findings.title: Parent 2FA switch state stays stale if the backup-codes dialog is dismissed without clicking Close
findings.body: Previously `onEnable()` was called immediately when the enable request succeeded; this PR replaces that with `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` and only calls `onEnable()` from the 'Close' button on the backup-codes screen. If the user dismisses the dialog any other way after enabling (the dialog's X, clicking the overlay, or pressing Escape — all of which trigger onOpenChange), onEnable is never invoked, so the two-factor switch in settings remains visually unchecked even though 2FA is now enabled server-side, until a page reload. The dialog-close path should also fire onEnable (or the parent should refresh state on open change once enablement succeeded).

findings.title: Read-modify-write race lets the same backup code authenticate concurrent requests
findings.body: Backup code consumption is decrypt → indexOf → set slot to null → re-encrypt → save, with no locking or atomic update. Two concurrent login requests using the same backup code can both read the pre-consumption ciphertext, both find the code, and both succeed before either writes back. One-time-use of a backup code is therefore not guaranteed under concurrent requests. Consider consuming the code inside a transaction with a re-read (e.g., `prisma.$transaction` with serializable isolation) or verifying after update that the slot was still present.

findings.title: Consumed backup codes are nulled in place instead of removed
findings.body: After a successful backup-code login the code does `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypts the array, leaving permanent `null` holes in the stored list. As a result the array never shrinks: once all ten codes are used the stored value is still truthy, so the user gets IncorrectBackupCode forever instead of MissingBackupCodes, and the stored blob accumulates dead entries. Splicing the entry out (`backupCodes.splice(index, 1)`) would keep the data clean and let the existing MissingBackupCodes error fire correctly when the list is empty.

findings.title: No test actually exercises logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code
findings.body: The new e2e coverage only asserts that the backup-code screen appears after enabling 2FA and that the download/copy buttons work (with TODOs for the file and clipboard contents). The core security behavior added by this PR — that a backup code logs a user in, that it works only once, that the password is still required, and that disabling 2FA with a backup code works — is entirely untested (the author also checked 'I haven't added tests that prove my feature works', and the file itself carries a TODO for it). The password-bypass and non-CAL-provider issues above would have been caught by such tests; at minimum a login-with-backup-code test and a single-use (second attempt fails) test should be added before merging.

findings.title: missing_backup_codes message tells users to 'generate them in your settings' but no such regeneration UI exists
findings.body: The added copy for `missing_backup_codes` reads 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' This PR adds no way to regenerate backup codes from settings — codes are only created during the 2FA setup flow, so the only way to get new ones is to disable and re-enable 2FA (which itself may require a backup code in the lost-access flow). The message directs users to an action that doesn't exist; it should be reworded (e.g., instruct them to contact support or reconfigure two-factor authentication).
